{"guardrail":"Horizon attribution is inference, not observation. {"guardrail":"M1 evidence may never upgrade a trade whose H4 location was not already valid.","lesson":"The H4 defines the arena a trade lives in. The M1 defines only the moment of entry. Confusing the two produces trades with correct timing inside the wrong arena.","practice":"Fix the arena first: H4 range, H4 direction of last decisive close, H4 level in play. Then let M1 answer one narrow question about when.","principle_id":"principle_013_h4_defines_arena_m1_defines_timing"}

{"guardrail":"Do not treat a large H4 body as evidence of participation until the internal path has been checked.","lesson":"Every H4 candle is exactly the aggregation of the H1, M15, M5 and M1 candles inside it. Nothing appears on the H4 that was not first built on the M1. The influence claim runs the other way from the construction.","practice":"When an H4 candle looks decisive, open the M15 inside it and check whether the body was built steadily or in one spike. Same H4 candle, very different meaning.","principle_id":"principle_014_nested_candle_composition"}

{"guardrail":"Never record a developing higher-timeframe candle as if it had closed. {"guardrail":"Early extremes and late extremes carry different implications; do not treat them as the same evidence.","lesson":"The H1 shows how the current H4 candle is being assembled: which side of the H4 open price is holding, and whether the H4 extremes were made early or late.","practice":"Locate the current price against the H4 open. {"guardrail":"A clean M15 path inside a hostile H4 location is still a hostile trade.","lesson":"M30 and M15 are the path layer. {"guardrail":"Alignment does not create an edge on its own. Stacked agreeing indicators are not independent evidence.","lesson":"Alignment across timeframes is a confidence input, not a signal. {"guardrail":"A lower-timeframe level inside a higher-timeframe void is a decoration, not a location.","lesson":"A level drawn from a higher timeframe survives more tests and attracts more resting orders than one drawn from a lower timeframe. {"guardrail":"Any decision record whose H4 bias is justified by M5 or M1 behavior is structurally invalid regardless of outcome.","lesson":"Lower-timeframe momentum does not establish higher-timeframe direction. {"guardrail":"A target that exceeds the plausible remaining higher-timeframe range is not ambitious, it is unfunded.","lesson":"Higher-timeframe realized range is the best available estimate of how far the lower timeframe can travel. {"guardrail":"Never justify holding a losing position by appealing to the higher timeframe while the lower timeframe invalidation has already printed.","lesson":"The high-to-low influence asymmetry is a tendency measured over many observations, not a law that holds in every window. {"guardrail":"Unlabeled structural claims should be treated as missing evidence, not as weak evidence.","lesson":"A single price can be an extreme on one timeframe and the middle of a range on another. {"guardrail":"The seasonality is in activity and range. It does not encode direction.","lesson":"Activity and volatility follow a repeatable daily shape tied to Tokyo, London and New York hours. This periodicity is one of the best-established facts about intraday currency and metals trading.","practice":"Timestamp every observation with its session. Compare a move to what that session normally does, not to a flat all-hours average.","principle_id":"principle_027_session_seasonality_is_real"}

{"principle_id":"principle_036_the_juke_is_folklore_with_a_real_mechanism","source_policy":"Distilled from human doctrine, trading literature principles and published empirical research; no copied book text.","task":"Learn one market-structure principle before reading chart examples.","topic":"the session-open false move"}

{"guardrail":"Do not attribute intent. {"principle_id":"principle_040_wide_spreads_at_opens","source_policy":"Distilled from human doctrine, trading literature principles and published empirical research; no copied book text.","task":"Learn one market-structure principle before reading chart examples.","topic":"spread behavior around session opens"}

{"guardrail":"A setup that only works at the tightest spread of the day is not a setup; it is a cost artifact.","lesson":"Spreads widen around session opens and in thin hours. The same nominal stop distance buys less protection at those moments.","practice":"Adjust the geometry check for the spread regime of the current session before validating a trade, not after.","principle_id":"principle_040_wide_spreads_at_opens"}

evidence_basis: Justified by liquidity and spread evidence rather than by a test of the rule itself; thin-hour execution costs are well documented.
evidence_sources: Ito and Hashimoto (2006)
BIS Triennial Central Bank Survey

{"principle_id":"principle_041_off_session_skip","source_policy":"Distilled from human doctrine, trading literature principles and published empirical research; no copied book text.","task":"Learn one market-structure principle before reading chart examples.","topic":"trading outside permitted sessions"}

{"guardrail":"Never let a compelling-looking setup override a session constraint. The constraint exists because setup quality is not measurable in thin liquidity.","lesson":"A session rule that forbids trading is a hard constraint and outranks any quality of setup found inside the forbidden window.","practice":"When the session rule blocks a trade, record the skip with the reason code and still write the structural observation. The observation remains useful training data.","principle_id":"principle_041_off_session_skip"}

evidence_basis: Studies of the pre-2015 London afternoon gold benchmark reported a directional skew in large moves during the window. The authors acknowledged no clear mechanism, and benign explanations involving liquidity and US data timing exist.
evidence_sources: Published analyses of London PM gold benchmark price behavior, 2004-2013

messages.content: Teach compact XAUUSD market-structure principles for later LoRA examples.

{"principle_id":"principle_042_gold_london_afternoon_anomaly","source_policy":"Distilled from human doctrine, trading literature principles and published empirical research; no copied book text.","task":"Learn one market-structure principle before reading chart examples.","topic":"gold-specific session anomaly"}

{"guardrail":"A historical statistical anomaly around a benchmark that has since changed is weak grounds for present-day directional expectation.","lesson":"Gold has one documented session-linked statistical anomaly, concentrated in the London afternoon benchmark window. Its cause is disputed and the benchmark mechanism has since been restructured.","practice":"Note the London afternoon window as a period of elevated event risk for gold specifically. Do not build a directional rule from it.","principle_id":"principle_042_gold_london_afternoon_anomaly"}

evidence_basis: Rests on the documented distinction between profit-taking reversals at a level and stop-triggered acceleration beyond it.
evidence_sources: Osler (2003); Osler (2005)

messages.content: Teach compact XAUUSD market-structure principles for later LoRA examples.

{"principle_id":"principle_043_sweep_versus_breakout","source_policy":"Distilled from human doctrine, trading literature principles and published empirical research; no copied book text.","task":"Learn one market-structure principle before reading chart examples.","topic":"distinguishing a sweep from a break"}

{"guardrail":"Classification requires the candle to be closed. A candle in progress can be either one until it finishes.","lesson":"Exceeding a level and accepting beyond it are different events. A wick through with a close back inside is a sweep; a close beyond with follow-through is a break.","practice":"Classify from the closed candle: where the extreme went, where the close landed, and what the next closed candle did relative to the level.","principle_id":"principle_043_sweep_versus_breakout"}

evidence_basis: Central construct of auction-market doctrine, where value is defined by trade occurring over time at a price rather than by the extreme reached.
evidence_sources: Auction market theory / market profile doctrine

messages.content: Teach compact XAUUSD market-structure principles for later LoRA examples.

{"principle_id":"principle_044_acceptance_requires_time","source_policy":"Distilled from human doctrine, trading literature principles and published empirical research; no copied book text.","task":"Learn one market-structure principle before reading chart examples.","topic":"acceptance versus rejection"}

{"guardrail":"A single large candle beyond a level is distance without duration. Do not label it acceptance.","lesson":"Acceptance is trade occurring beyond a level over time. Rejection is a fast return. The distinguishing variable is duration and volume beyond the level, not distance.","practice":"Measure how many closed candles traded beyond the level and how much volume they carried before calling it acceptance.","principle_id":"principle_044_acceptance_requires_time"}

evidence_basis: Consistent with effort-versus-result doctrine in tape-reading and volume analysis traditions; direct quantitative validation is limited.
evidence_sources: Tape-reading and volume-analysis doctrine (Wyckoff tradition)

messages.content: Teach compact XAUUSD market-structure principles for later LoRA examples.

{"principle_id":"principle_045_volume_confirms_participation_not_direction","source_policy":"Distilled from human doctrine, trading literature principles and published empirical research; no copied book text.","task":"Learn one market-structure principle before reading chart examples.","topic":"volume at a level"}

{"guardrail":"Low volume weakens both the bull and bear case at a level; it does not favor either.","lesson":"Volume tells you how many participants engaged, not which side won. High volume on a rejection and high volume on a break mean opposite things.","practice":"Always pair a volume observation with the closed-candle location it accompanied. Never cite volume alone as evidence.","principle_id":"principle_045_volume_confirms_participation_not_direction"}

evidence_basis: Compatible with the order-clustering mechanism: a break that exhausts the stop cluster without attracting continuation flow reverts.
evidence_sources: Osler (2005); auction-market rejection doctrine

messages.content: Teach compact XAUUSD market-structure principles for later LoRA examples.

{"principle_id":"principle_046_failed_break_is_high_information","source_policy":"Distilled from human doctrine, trading literature principles and published empirical research; no copied book text.","task":"Learn one market-structure principle before reading chart examples.","topic":"failed breaks"}

{"guardrail":"The information arrives only when the failure is confirmed by a closed candle back inside. Anticipating a failure is not the same as observing one.","lesson":"A break that fails carries more information than a break that continues, because it reveals that orders on the far side of the level were insufficient to hold the new price.","practice":"When a break fails, upgrade the surviving level's rank and note the failure as a tested response.","principle_id":"principle_046_failed_break_is_high_information"}

evidence_basis: Practitioner classification; no located quantitative test separating retest types by outcome.
evidence_sources: Practitioner price-action doctrine; untested

{"principle_id":"principle_047_retest_quality","source_policy":"Distilled from human doctrine, trading literature principles and published empirical research; no copied book text.","task":"Learn one market-structure principle before reading chart examples.","topic":"retest quality"}

{"guardrail":"'It retested' is not a finding. The finding is how it retested.","lesson":"Not all retests are equal. A retest that arrives quickly with small candles is different evidence from one that arrives slowly after a deep pullback.","practice":"Record time elapsed, depth of the return and candle size on the retest, then rate the retest rather than merely noting that one occurred.","principle_id":"principle_047_retest_quality"}

evidence_basis: Standard statistical point about correlated predictors, and a central theme in evidence-based critiques of technical analysis.
evidence_sources: Aronson-style evidence-based technical analysis critique

{"principle_id":"principle_048_confluence_is_not_addition","source_policy":"Distilled from human doctrine, trading literature principles and published empirical research; no copied book text.","task":"Learn one market-structure principle before reading chart examples.","topic":"counting confluence"}

{"guardrail":"Long confluence lists usually signal correlated redundancy rather than strong evidence.","lesson":"Several correlated observations pointing the same way are close to one observation, not several. Independence is what makes evidence add up.","practice":"Before counting a factor as confirmation, ask whether it could have disagreed with the factors already counted. If not, do not count it.","principle_id":"principle_048_confluence_is_not_addition"}

evidence_basis: Consistent with evidence that documented market patterns decay as participants and technology adapt.
evidence_sources: Evidence on decay of documented FX inefficiencies over time

messages.content: Teach compact XAUUSD market-structure principles for later LoRA examples.

{"principle_id":"principle_049_level_needs_current_response","source_policy":"Distilled from human doctrine, trading literature principles and published empirical research; no copied book text.","task":"Learn one market-structure principle before reading chart examples.","topic":"levels require current confirmation"}

{"guardrail":"Historical significance decays. A level untested for a long period should be ranked lower, not higher.","lesson":"A level's history establishes candidacy. Only a current closed-price response establishes that it is still active.","practice":"Require at least one current closed-candle response before allowing a historical level to justify a trade.","principle_id":"principle_049_level_needs_current_response"}

evidence_basis: This is the single-trade version of data-snooping bias, which is the best-documented failure mode in technical rule evaluation.
evidence_sources: Sullivan, Timmermann, White (1999), Data-Snooping, Technical Trading Rule Performance, and the Bootstrap, Journal of Finance

messages.content: Teach compact XAUUSD market-structure principles for later LoRA examples.

{"principle_id":"principle_050_structure_break_needs_a_frame","source_policy":"Distilled from human doctrine, trading literature principles and published empirical research; no copied book text.","task":"Learn one market-structure principle before reading chart examples.","topic":"defining a structure break"}

{"guardrail":"Changing the swing definition after the fact to produce a break is curve fitting inside a single trade.","lesson":"A break of structure is only meaningful once the swing points that define the structure are stated. Different swing definitions produce different breaks on the same chart.","practice":"State the swing points and the timeframe before declaring a break. Keep the swing definition constant across a decision series.","principle_id":"principle_050_structure_break_needs_a_frame"}

evidence_basis: A landmark study tested thousands of technical rules across a century of index data and found none survived a bootstrap correction for data-snooping bias on the out-of-sample period.
evidence_sources: Sullivan, Timmermann, White (1999), Journal of Finance

messages.content: Teach compact XAUUSD market-structure principles for later LoRA examples.

{"principle_id":"principle_051_data_snooping_bias","source_policy":"Distilled from human doctrine, trading literature principles and published empirical research; no copied book text.","task":"Learn one market-structure principle before reading chart examples.","topic":"why most discovered patterns fail"}

{"guardrail":"A rule with an impressive backtest and no correction for the number of rules tried should be assigned low confidence regardless of how good the curve looks.","lesson":"When many rules are searched over the same history, some will look excellent by chance alone. Correcting for that search is what separates a finding from a coincidence.","practice":"Record how many variants were considered before a rule was adopted. Treat unrecorded search as unbounded search.","principle_id":"principle_051_data_snooping_bias"}

evidence_basis: Published intraday momentum results report in-sample and out-of-sample explanatory power on the order of one to two percent.
evidence_sources: Gao, Han, Li, Zhou (2018), Journal of Financial Economics

{"principle_id":"principle_052_effects_are_small_when_real","source_policy":"Distilled from human doctrine, trading literature principles and published empirical research; no copied book text.","task":"Learn one market-structure principle before reading chart examples.","topic":"calibrating effect size"}

{"guardrail":"Any framework that implies a high win rate from a single structural observation is misrepresenting the evidence base it claims to rest on.","lesson":"Where intraday and session effects have been rigorously measured, they explain a very small share of variance. Real edges in this domain are thin, not obvious.","practice":"Express expected edge in small increments. Reserve high confidence for cases with multiple independent strong-evidence supports.","principle_id":"principle_052_effects_are_small_when_real"}

evidence_basis: Academic breakout research reports profitability concentrated in a high-volatility sub-period and explicitly not robust across time.
evidence_sources: Holmberg, Lonnbark, Lundstrom (2013), Finance Research Letters

{"principle_id":"principle_053_regime_dependence","source_policy":"Distilled from human doctrine, trading literature principles and published empirical research; no copied book text.","task":"Learn one market-structure principle before reading chart examples.","topic":"edges are regime-dependent"}

{"guardrail":"A pooled average across regimes can hide the fact that the rule only ever worked in one of them.","lesson":"Strategies that test positively often concentrate their entire result in one volatility regime and disappear in others. Stability across regimes is a separate question from average profitability.","practice":"Tag every decision with the prevailing volatility regime so results can later be split by regime rather than pooled.","principle_id":"principle_053_regime_dependence"}

evidence_basis: Realized-volatility models perform strongly on gold and FX, and this literature positions the output as a risk-regime and sizing input rather than a source of directional alpha.
evidence_sources: Corsi (2009); HAR-type applications to gold futures realized volatility

messages.content: Teach compact XAUUSD market-structure principles for later LoRA examples.

{"principle_id":"principle_054_volatility_forecast_to_sizing","source_policy":"Distilled from human doctrine, trading literature principles and published empirical research; no copied book text.","task":"Learn one market-structure principle before reading chart examples.","topic":"using volatility forecasts correctly"}

{"guardrail":"Confusing a volatility regime signal for a directional signal is the most common misapplication of the cross-timeframe evidence.","lesson":"Good volatility forecasting is genuinely achievable and belongs in position sizing and stop placement. It does not convert into directional forecasting.","practice":"Route every volatility estimate into size and geometry. Route no volatility estimate into direction.","principle_id":"principle_054_volatility_forecast_to_sizing"}

evidence_basis: Cost sensitivity is a recurring finding wherever intraday rules are tested properly; informal breakout tests report per-trade profit near zero before costs.
evidence_sources: Holmberg et al. (2013)
Public breakout backtests reporting near-zero per-trade profit

{"principle_id":"principle_055_costs_decide_marginal_setups","source_policy":"Distilled from human doctrine, trading literature principles and published empirical research; no copied book text.","task":"Learn one market-structure principle before reading chart examples.","topic":"transaction costs"}

{"guardrail":"Gross-of-cost reasoning makes weak rules look tradeable and is a standard way backtests mislead.","lesson":"Spread and slippage decide the fate of marginal setups. A rule with a small gross edge and ordinary costs is a losing rule.","practice":"Subtract a realistic round-trip cost before rating any setup as acceptable, and use the session-appropriate spread rather than a best-case one.","principle_id":"principle_055_costs_decide_marginal_setups"}

evidence_basis: Applies directly to the session-open false-move pattern and to multi-timeframe filtering, neither of which has a located rigorous test.
evidence_sources: Evidence survey conducted for this curriculum

{"principle_id":"principle_056_absence_of_evidence_is_information","source_policy":"Distilled from human doctrine, trading literature principles and published empirical research; no copied book text.","task":"Learn one market-structure principle before reading chart examples.","topic":"acting on untested patterns"}

{"guardrail":"An untested pattern may be observed and logged. It may not carry a trade on its own.","lesson":"When a pattern has never been tested rigorously, that absence is itself a fact worth recording. It is not the same as the pattern being false, and it is not the same as the pattern being supported.","practice":"Label each pattern the system uses with its evidence status. Let the label affect confidence and size directly.","principle_id":"principle_056_absence_of_evidence_is_information"}

evidence_basis: Multiple widely taught session and structure concepts were found to have no sample sizes, win rates or out-of-sample tests published anywhere.
evidence_sources: Evidence survey conducted for this curriculum

{"principle_id":"principle_057_popularity_is_not_evidence","source_policy":"Distilled from human doctrine, trading literature principles and published empirical research; no copied book text.","task":"Learn one market-structure principle before reading chart examples.","topic":"widely taught is not tested"}

{"guardrail":"Community consensus is a social fact, not a market fact.","lesson":"The number of people teaching a pattern says nothing about whether it works. Widely repeated practitioner concepts frequently have no empirical record at all.","practice":"Separate the source of a concept from the evidence for it. Record both fields independently.","principle_id":"principle_057_popularity_is_not_evidence"}

evidence_basis: Grounded in behavioral critiques of narrative construction and hindsight-driven pattern seeking.
evidence_sources: Behavioral finance critiques of narrative and hindsight bias

{"principle_id":"principle_058_no_intent_attribution","source_policy":"Distilled from human doctrine, trading literature principles and published empirical research; no copied book text.","task":"Learn one market-structure principle before reading chart examples.","topic":"describing rather than narrating"}

{"guardrail":"Intent narratives feel explanatory and increase confidence without increasing information. That combination is dangerous.","lesson":"Describe what price did. Do not narrate why an unseen participant supposedly did it. Intent is unobservable and adds no predictive content.","practice":"Write observations as sequences of closed-candle facts at named levels. Reserve interpretation for a clearly separate field.","principle_id":"principle_058_no_intent_attribution"}

evidence_basis: Selection and survivorship effects are among the best-documented reasons that apparent trading patterns fail out of sample.
evidence_sources: Sullivan, Timmermann, White (1999); evidence-based technical analysis critique

{"principle_id":"principle_059_sample_before_belief","source_policy":"Distilled from human doctrine, trading literature principles and published empirical research; no copied book text.","task":"Learn one market-structure principle before reading chart examples.","topic":"when a pattern earns weight"}

{"guardrail":"Logging only the occurrences that were traded, or only the ones that worked, destroys the sample before it exists.","lesson":"A pattern earns weight after a pre-specified number of independent observations have been logged and reviewed, not after a memorable example.","practice":"Set the required sample size before starting to collect. Log every occurrence, including the ones that failed and the ones that were skipped.","principle_id":"principle_059_sample_before_belief"}

evidence_basis: Follows from the combination of the small measured effect sizes, the regime dependence and the data-snooping findings recorded elsewhere in this stage.
evidence_sources: Synthesis of principles 051-059

{"principle_id":"principle_060_confidence_must_track_evidence","source_policy":"Distilled from human doctrine, trading literature principles and published empirical research; no copied book text.","task":"Learn one market-structure principle before reading chart examples.","topic":"calibrating stated confidence"}

{"guardrail":"A visually perfect setup built entirely on untested doctrine is a low-confidence trade. Chart aesthetics are not evidence.","lesson":"Stated confidence must be a function of the evidence class behind the decision. Strong-evidence supports earn higher confidence; untested supports do not, however clean the chart looks.","practice":"Map each decision's supporting principles to their evidence strength, and let the weakest critical link cap the confidence score.","principle_id":"principle_060_confidence_must_track_evidence"}
